name: Ibzan
overview: Ibzan was a male judge of Israel who served in this role for seven years, as recorded in Judges 12:8. His leadership contributed to the period of governance during the time of the judges, a crucial era in Israel's history. Scripture identifies him specifically by his role rather than tribal affiliation or family background.
namesAndTitles: The name Ibzan means 'swift,' reflecting a proper name recorded in Judges 12:8. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it serves as his identifying personal name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Ibzan beyond his role as a judge of Israel. There are no additional relational details provided about his lineage or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Ibzan's significance lies in his leadership as a judge over Israel for seven years, a period during which he would have provided guidance and governance to the people. His mention in Judges highlights the ongoing cycle of judges raised by God to lead Israel in times of need. Though details about his deeds are limited, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in raising leaders to preserve His covenant people.
